questions.question: Unix command to change file permissions using numeric notation.
questions.explanation: chmod modifies read, write, and execute permissions.

questions.question: File system structure containing metadata about files.
questions.explanation: Inodes store information about files in Unix file systems.

questions.question: Link that creates a mirror entry in the file system pointing to the same data.
questions.explanation: Hard links create additional directory entries for the same file.

questions.question: Unix command to find files in a directory hierarchy.
questions.explanation: The find command searches for files based on various criteria.

questions.question: Reclaiming SSD blocks no longer in use.
questions.explanation: TRIM tells the SSD which blocks are deleted so its internal garbage collection can reclaim them in advance, preserving write performance.

questions.question: Condition where a file's blocks are scattered non-contiguously.
questions.explanation: Fragmentation occurs when files are split across scattered blocks.

questions.question: Table tracking free and used space on a disk.
questions.explanation: FAT is a file system method tracking cluster allocation.

questions.question: Unix permission notation using letters for read, write, execute.
questions.explanation: Symbolic notation uses r, w, x for permissions.

questions.question: Process of reorganizing disk data to improve access speed.
questions.explanation: Defragmentation consolidates fragmented files for better performance.

questions.question: Unix command to change file ownership.
questions.explanation: chown modifies the owner and group of files.

questions.question: What permission set does chmod 755 grant in symbolic form?
alternatives: owner rwx, group and others r-x
questions.explanation: 7 (4+2+1) gives the owner read/write/execute; 5 (4+1) gives group and others read/execute only.

questions.question: Unix command that searches file contents for lines matching a pattern.
questions.explanation: grep prints lines matching a string or regex, e.g. grep 'error' app.log.

questions.question: Unix command that bundles multiple files into a .tar archive.
questions.explanation: tar (tape archive) packs files into one archive; combined with gzip it makes .tar.gz files.

questions.question: File system technique that logs changes before applying them to prevent corruption.
questions.explanation: A journal records pending operations so the file system can recover cleanly after a crash; ext4 and NTFS use it.

questions.question: Special Unix permission making a program run with its file owner's privileges.
questions.explanation: The setuid bit lets a program execute with the owner's rights, which is how passwd can modify protected files.

questions.question: A shared document must be readable and writable only by its owner, and merely readable by group and everyone else. Give the chmod numeric permission.
questions.explanation: 6 = read+write for the owner, 4 = read for the group, 4 = read for others — the standard permission for shared documents.

questions.question: A flash drive shows 20 GB free, yet copying a single 6 GB video fails because the drive is formatted FAT32. What limitation causes this?
questions.explanation: FAT32 cannot store a single file larger than 4 GB (technically 4 GiB minus 1 byte) no matter how much free space remains.

questions.question: Files named report-3-5-24 and report-12-2-23 sort out of order in a folder. Which date naming convention makes alphabetical sorting match chronological order?
questions.explanation: Leading with the year, then zero-padded month and day (e.g. 2024-03-05), makes name sorting equal date sorting.

questions.question: A Linux server's disk is nearly full and the admin must find which directory consumes the most space. Which command reports disk usage per directory?
questions.explanation: du (disk usage) summarizes space per file or directory; 'du -sh /var/*' reveals the biggest folders at a glance.

questions.question: After an improper shutdown, Windows automatically scans the drive's file system for errors on the next boot. Which built-in utility performs this check?
questions.explanation: chkdsk (Check Disk) scans for and repairs file system corruption caused by crashes or power loss.
